prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, using bifunctional PROTACs and the mechanism of molecular glue degraders to direct E3 ubiquitin ligases to chosen proteins

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is a chemical idea that can be stated in one sentence: a small molecule that brings a target protein and an E3 ligase together makes the cell destroy the protein, so drug action becomes event-driven and catalytic instead of occupancy-driven. The PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies, with Sakamoto) and Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target, which explains molecular glue degraders, give a coherent prize with a design strand and a mechanistic strand. Seven of eight members ranked it in their top five, which suggests this is the least divisive option rather than the narrowest favourite. The field has been confirmed independently by many laboratories and has reached targets that occupancy-based inhibitors could not.
statement.case_against: The attribution problem is real. Eight names are credited and any trio leaves out Sakamoto, Ciulli, Gray, Kim and Ito, whose contributions are not minor. The glue and PROTAC strands also have different histories, because lenalidomide worked clinically before its mechanism was known. Clinical vindication by an approved bifunctional degrader is, as far as the colleagues and I can tell, still pending, so the committee could be a few years early. If it is early, Buchwald-Hartwig (B005) is the safer choice on maturity and on the clean two-person attribution.

responses.point: Ranked B037 fifth and judged recognition perhaps a few years early because clinical outcomes of degraders are not yet established, while placing Car-Parrinello (B016) first as long overdue and cleanly attributed.
responses.response: I accept the maturity concern, and it is why I name B005 as an alternative. But the Nobel criterion is the chemical discovery and its demonstrated reproducibility, not the approval record of a drug class. PROTACs have been reproduced widely over two decades and cereblon-based glues are already established medicines, so the concept is validated even if no bifunctional degrader is yet approved. I agree B016 has the cleanest credit of any shortlisted entry, and I would not oppose it as an alternative. My hesitation is that it is a method for simulation, and I think the committee will find it harder to argue for its chemical consequences than for a new modality.

responses.point: Proposed Crews, Handa and Ciulli for B037, crediting Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex cooperativity, and ranked genetic code expansion (B002) first.
responses.response: I take the Ciulli case seriously, since his VHL ligands made PROTACs drug-like and he gave the mechanistic basis for cooperativity. I still prefer Deshaies in the third slot because Crews and Deshaies together conceived and first demonstrated the heterobifunctional degrader, which is the founding act, while Ciulli's work is a decisive refinement of it. I admit that is a judgement and I would not call it settled. On B002 I disagree with ranking it first. The discovery is elegant, but credit among Schultz, Wang, Chin, Mehl and Yokoyama is as entangled as in B037, and its impact is as a tool for protein research rather than as a new way to make medicines.

responses.point: Ranked B005 first, arguing that C-N coupling is broad, mechanistically clear and overdue, with Kosugi's tin-amide chemistry a precursor but not the decisive step.
responses.response: I agree with the attribution and with the overdue point, and as a synthetic chemist I put B005 second. My reservation is the relationship to 2010: the palladium C-C coupling prize already honoured the idea that Pd catalysis forges bonds between fragments, and C-N coupling is its most important extension but still an extension in concept. B037 opens a different kind of chemistry. I would not call B005 a poor choice, and if the committee prefers certainty on credit and maturity I could support it.

responses.point: Ranked base editing (B060) first as a molecular-design invention with Liu alone as laureate, and judged the CRISPR prize of 2020 not to be a bar.
responses.response: I agree on Liu alone and on the chemistry of deaminase fusions, which is why I had it third. But I think the CRISPR overlap is more serious than you suggest: base editing is largely a specific engineering of a tool the 2020 prize recognised, and the Nishida and Kondo parallel report remains an attribution issue. Degraders carry no comparable precedent prize. If we separate the two, B037 has less of a precedent problem and B060 less of a crowding problem, and I would rank B037 higher.

uncertainties: Whether the prize should centre on PROTACs, on molecular glues, or on both, and whether Ciulli or Sakamoto should replace Deshaies or Handa.
Whether the absence of an approved bifunctional degrader makes the timing premature relative to B005 or B016.
Whether the committee regards Buchwald-Hartwig as sufficiently distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate. I have no recorded tie to the credited names. Lund colleagues (Linke, Sparr) and my Masamune training are not connected to any shortlisted ballot.
